modules.description: An arbitrary MongoDB command, run as given against one mongod.
modules.name: command

run.description:
Run a raw command against MongoDB via db.runCommand (imperative verb-action).
Defaults to changed=false (probe); the operator is responsible for idempotency.
Output.ok — success flag of the response. No dry-run preview.

changed.description: Mark the result as changed=true (for commands that actually mutate state). Defaults to false (probe semantics).

command.description: bson document of the command (first/only key — the command name), e.g. { serverStatus: 1 } or { collStats: "events" }. For PILOT — single-field commands.

password.description: MongoDB password (vault ref; keeper resolves before Apply). Masked — is not passed into the command arguments (goes into the connection).

tls.description: Connect over TLS. Defaults to false. PILOT: mongo in plain — not set.

tls_ca.description: CA PEM for verifying the server certificate. Masked (secret).

tls_cert.description: Client-cert PEM for mTLS (optional, with tls_key). Masked (secret).

tls_key.description: Client-key PEM for mTLS (optional, with tls_cert). Masked (secret).

tls_skip_verify.description: EXPLICIT opt-out of certificate verification. Defaults to false (default secure).

modules.description: A live mongod: the health probe that gates everything a scenario does after it.
modules.name: instance

pinged.description:
MongoDB health probe via go-mongo-driver Ping (primary). Read-only,
changed=false by design (probe, not a mutation). Output.ok — condition for the
health gate (until: register.self.ok == true). No dry-run preview.

password.description: MongoDB password (vault ref in operator-input; keeper resolves before Apply). Masked — does not end up in events/logs. Not passed to Ping (goes into the connection).

tls.description: Connect to mongod over TLS. Defaults to false (plaintext). PILOT: mongo in plain mode — not set.

tls_ca.description: PEM of the CA certificate for verifying the server certificate (RootCAs). Masked (secret). Resolved keeper-side from Vault (render phase).

tls_cert.description: PEM of the client certificate for mTLS (optional, only together with tls_key). Masked (secret).

tls_key.description: PEM of the client key for mTLS (optional, only together with tls_cert). Masked (secret); does not end up in events/errors.

tls_skip_verify.description: EXPLICIT opt-out of server certificate verification. Defaults to false (verification enabled — default secure).

username.description: ACL username for AUTH (if not anonymous).

modules.description: One MongoDB user of a live mongod, reconciled through createUser / dropUser.
modules.name: user

absent.description:
Remove a MongoDB user via dropUser (go-mongo-driver). Idempotent via usersInfo:
a user the instance does not have is a no-op (changed=false).

The localhost-exception fallback of `present` does NOT apply here: removing a
user requires privileges, so an auth failure is a failure and not a bootstrap.
No dry-run preview.

database.description: The DB the user lives in (default admin). dropUser runs in this DB's context.

name.description: MongoDB username to remove. This is the SUBJECT of the step, not the user to authenticate as (that is `username`).

password.description: Password of the ADMIN CONNECTION under which the user is removed (vault ref, keeper resolves before Apply). Goes into the connection credentials; does not end up in events/logs.

tls.description: Connect over TLS. Defaults to false. PILOT: mongo in plain — not set.

tls_ca.description: CA PEM for verifying the server certificate. Masked (secret).

tls_cert.description: Client-cert PEM for mTLS (optional, with tls_key). Masked (secret).

tls_key.description: Client-key PEM for mTLS (optional, with tls_cert). Masked (secret).

tls_skip_verify.description: EXPLICIT opt-out of certificate verification. Defaults to false (default secure).

username.description: ACL username for the AUTH connection (the admin under which the user is removed).

present.description:
Create a MongoDB user via createUser (go-mongo-driver). Idempotent via
usersInfo: a user that already exists is a no-op (changed=false) — changing the
password or roles of an existing user is day-2, out of PILOT scope. ★ the first
admin is created via the localhost-exception (no-auth loopback connection, while
the admin DB is empty). No dry-run preview.

database.description: The DB in which the user is created (login/roles context). Default admin (system users). Roles without an explicit db inherit this DB.

name.description: MongoDB username to create. This is the SUBJECT of the step, not the user to authenticate as (that is `username`).

password.description: Password of the ADMIN CONNECTION (the user is created under username; vault ref, keeper resolves before Apply). Goes into the connection credentials; does not end up in events/logs. ★ This is NOT the password of the user being created (see user_password) — except for bootstrapping the first admin, where the admin creates ITSELF (password serves both roles when user_password is not set).

roles.description: User roles (array of {role, db}). Each element — {role: "readWrite", db: "appdb"}. db with no value inherits database. Must be non-empty (a user without roles is meaningless).

tls.description: Connect over TLS. Defaults to false. PILOT: mongo in plain — not set.

tls_ca.description: CA PEM for verifying the server certificate. Masked (secret).

tls_cert.description: Client-cert PEM for mTLS (optional, with tls_key). Masked (secret).

tls_key.description: Client-key PEM for mTLS (optional, with tls_cert). Masked (secret).

tls_skip_verify.description: EXPLICIT opt-out of certificate verification. Defaults to false (default secure).

user_password.description: Password of the CREATED user (pwd of the createUser document; vault ref, keeper resolves before Apply). Separate from password (admin connection auth): for operator users the connection is under the admin password, while createUser uses this password. Not set → falls back to password (bootstrap of the first admin: the admin creates itself under the same password). Masked.

username.description: ACL username for the AUTH connection (the admin under which the user is created). During bootstrap of the first admin, auth is not yet possible → localhost-exception no-auth.
